channel.title: Doc Radar
channel.description: Upcoming documentary releases from the distributors, broadcasters, streamers and sales agents that matter. Updated weekly.

item.title: Welcome to the Family: The Murder of Dan Markel
item.description: How far would you go for your family? The brutal murder of a prominent law professor in Tallahassee, Florida reveals the dark secrets of a wealthy family. A series of larger-than-life suspects leads to a mind-bending story of a murder-for-hire-plot, a messy custody battle, ex-lovers – and family dentistry. With exclusive access to those at the center of this extraordinary story, many of whom have never spoken before, this is the definitive telling of a case which took 11 years to solve.

item.title: Windows on the World: 9/11's Forgotten Story
item.description: Directed by Yeen Nie Hoe. Twenty-five years after 9/11, this gripping documentary tells the untold story of the 170 people trapped inside Windows on the World, the iconic restaurant on the top floors of the World Trade Center’s North Tower.

item.title: Untold Raygun: Breaking Badly (Netflix)
item.description: Directed by Chapman Way. Nobody, least of all Rachael Gunn, expected to be an Olympian. But as Raygun’s performance at the 2024 Paris Olympics went viral overnight, so did an avalanche of memes, misinformation, and conspiracy theories questioning how she ever got there.

item.title: Achill Island
item.description: Life on Achill Island, off County Mayo – shark fishing, shepherding, pottery making, teaching, B&B-ing and socialising in the pub by night.

item.title: Turning Point: Generation 9/11 (Netflix)
item.description: Directed by Brian Knappenberger. A quarter-century after September 11th, the attacks' ripple effects persist across generations. Orphaned children, War on Terror journalists, young Afghans, and U.S. Marines shaped by the 2021 withdrawal share their stories.

item.title: SUMO: Spirit Weighs Nothing (ESPN Films / 30 for 30)
item.description: Directed by Erik Shirai. SUMO: Spirit Weighs Nothing grants rare inside access to Japan’s notoriously private world of sumo. Over a turbulent year of sacrifice and survival, wrestlers at different stages of their career fight to endure within one of Japan’s most punishing traditions. Behind the curtain, true strength is measured — not in flesh, but in refining the spirit.

item.title: Kuzma: Extremely Happy
item.description: Directed by Artem Hryhorian. Through exclusive archival footage and never before seen home video, this documentary aims to explore the real face of Andriy Viktorovych Kuzmenko (Kuzma Skryabin), the father of the contemporary Ukrainian rock and roll scene.

item.title: Fito Páez: The World Within a Song (Netflix)
item.description: Directed by Matías Gueilburt. A documentary film that observes, listens to, and interacts with Fito Páez from a place of profound intimacy. The camera, almost invisible, witnesses his every move, accompanying him for over a year during recordings, rehearsals, tours, and performances in major cities across Latin America, Europe, and the United States. It is also a journey through the life of one of the greatest Spanish-language artists: his loves and heartbreaks, children and friendships, excesses, tragedies, failures, and successes.

item.title: Super Nature
item.description: Directed by Ed Sayers. We’re invited on a journey across 25 different countries, with people embracing both abundance and loss, to feel a sense of togetherness with our fellow dwellers on earth, human and non-human. Celebrating all we have and reflecting on all we have to lose, Super Nature proposes a new way of seeing.

item.title: Celtic Utopia
item.description: Directed by Dennis Harvey. The story of a new Ireland and its vibrant music scene, but also that of a postcolonial society wrestling with its heritage. A society where folk music carries both the oppression of the past and the dream of a bright future.

item.title: Famous Last Words: Gloria Steinem (Netflix)
item.description: Before her death, activist Gloria Steinem shared her final, heartfelt message with the world, knowing this interview would not air until she was gone.

item.title: Fragments of Paradise
item.description: Directed by KD Davison. For over 70 years, Jonas Mekas, internationally known as the "godfather" of avant-garde cinema, documented his life in what came to be known as his diary films. From his arrival in New York City as a displaced person in 1949 to his death in 2019, he chronicled the trauma and loss of exile while pioneering institutions to support the growth of independent film in the United States. Fragments of Paradise is an intimate look at his life and work constructed from thousands of hours of his own video and film diaries-including never-before-seen tapes and unpublished audio recordings. It is a story about finding beauty amidst profound loss, and a man who tried to make sense of it all... with a camera.

item.title: Instadocs: The Decoy Plane (Netflix)
item.description: A critical threat. A clandestine escape. And a Turkish catering truck? With firsthand accounts, "Instadocs" digs into what happened aboard Air Force One.

item.title: Teenage Wasteland (Netflix)
item.description: Directed by Amanda McBaine. Inspired by an unconventional teacher, a group of teenagers in upstate New York in the early 1990s make a student film and uncover a vast conspiracy that is poisoning their community. Thirty years later, they revisit their film and confront the legacy of this transformative experience.

item.title: Nobody Here: The Story of Vaporwave
item.description: Directed by Christian Britten. ‘Nobody Here’ traces the story of Vaporwave and its evolution into the internet’s most aesthetic and celebrated micro-genre — from its origins in obscure online communities to its emergence in the mainstream consciousness.

item.title: The Club That Conquered the Premier League
item.description: The story of the local neighbourhood club, Antiguoko, that became a Basque dream team and helped produce Premier League managers Xabi Alonso, Mikel Arteta and Andoni Iraola.

item.title: Remake (PBS (POV & Independent Lens))
item.description: Directed by Ross McElwee. For nearly forty years, Ross McElwee has made autobiographical documentaries about how his personal life intersects with the wider world. After his son Adrian died of a fentanyl overdose in 2016, McElwee abandoned a planned Hollywood dramatic remake of his own 1986 breakthrough film Sherman's March, and instead used decades of home-movie footage — including Adrian's own camera work — to reckon with his son's life, his addiction, and what the camera did and did not capture.

item.title: OJ Unseen: Exploitation of Evil
item.description: A decade after O.J. Simpson was controversially acquitted of the murders of his ex-wife Nicole Brown Simpson and her friend Ron Goldman, he attempted to rebrand himself as a reality TV star with the hidden camera prank PPV special Juiced.

item.title: Lomu
item.description: Directed by Gavin FitzGerald. A Tongan/Kiwi warrior who could run 100 metres in under 11 seconds. He was the youngest All Black to put on the jersey and still holds the record for the most tries scored in World Cup history.

item.title: The Bodies on the Bridge
item.description: In July 2024, the discovery of the two suitcases containing human remains on Bristol’s Clifton Suspension Bridge shocked the nation and sparked one of the UK’s most disturbing murder investigations in recent memory.

item.title: They're Here (ARTE)
item.description: Directed by Laura Poitras. Edén Villa (pseudonym) and anonymous Minneapolis residents evade and resist the paramilitary occupation of their city, in a winter landscape where masked agents abduct children, residents travel in trunks, shackled prisoners are loaded onto airplanes within eyesight of vacationers, and bicyclists track the movements of an invading force.

item.title: Filling the void
item.description: Directed by Aaron Lecoublet. A portrait of Magali Garçon, a professor at the Cherbourg School of Arts, whose convictions, feminist vision, and committed personality challenge the traditional art academy, bringing a unique and transformative perspective to her teaching.

item.title: Untold Mr. T: I Pity the Fool (Netflix)
item.description: Directed by Scott Weintrob. Before the gold chains, mohawk, and Hollywood fame of The A-Team and Rocky III, there was Laurence Tureaud. This is the extraordinary origin story behind one of the most unlikely and beloved icons in entertainment — Mr. T.

item.title: Oasis: Don't Look Back in Anger
item.description: Directed by Dylan Southern. Experience the meteoric rise of Oasis through rare footage and untold stories as the band reunites for Oasis Live '25, chronicling their journey from Manchester streets to global rock stardom.

item.title: A Killer Story (HBO Documentary Films)
item.description: Investigative journalist Joe Sexton looks into a 2002 double homicide case in Kansas after receiving thousands of emails from Eileen Umbehr, a homemaker turned citizen sleuth. Eileen and her husband Keen are convinced that Dana Chandler, the woman accused of killing her ex-husband and his girlfriend, did not commit the crime and devote their lives to fighting for Chandler's innocence.

item.title: Secrets of the Bayeux Tapestry: Inside the Museum
item.description: Directed by Joe Myerscough. The Bayeux Tapestry is one of the treasures of the medieval world. Across 70 metres of exquisitely embroidered scenes, it tells the story of one of the most seismic events in British history – the Norman Invasion of 1066. For the last 950 years, this crucial part of Britain's national story has remained on the other side of the English Channel, in Bayeux, Normandy, but now it’s coming back to the UK. A stellar cast of historians and experts follow the painstaking efforts to bring this priceless work of art back to the UK, where experts believe it was made, for a once-in-a-millennium exhibition at the British Museum.

item.title: The Pandemic Prophet
item.description: Directed by Caroline Benarrosh. When Professor Didier Raoult promotes a "miracle cure" for COVID-19, six ordinary citizens go after the truth -- including his own daughter.

item.title: Pompeji - Die Villa von Neros Kaiserin (ARTE)
item.description: Directed by Daniel Oron.

item.title: Andy Goldsworthy in Conversation with Andrew Graham-Dixon
item.description: Directed by Andrew Graham-Dixon. Filmed entirely on-site at the National Galleries of Scotland during Goldsworthy's monumental 2025 retrospective, Andy Goldsworthy: 50 Years, this compelling film captures an exclusive, deeply personal dialogue between the world-renowned land artist and the acclaimed art historian, author, and broadcaster. The documentary offers an unprecedented look behind the scenes of Goldsworthy’s largest and most ambitious indoor exhibition. Surrounded by new installations created specifically for the show, the pair explore the core environmental philosophies, fleeting natural materials, and creative ideas that have defined the artist's extraordinary half-century career.

item.title: Le roi de Shanghai (ARTE)
item.description: Directed by Sandra Rude.

item.title: Dragging Up The Past
item.description: Cork’s long association with drag and its history is celebrated in Dragging Up The Past, a documentary utilising a mix of archival footage and interviews to showcase Cork City’s colourful drag community.

item.title: Steel: The Blood of Us
item.description: Directed by Joe Cornick. Steel: The Blood of Us is a cinematic love letter to the end of the industrial revolution, capturing the community of Port Talbot, Wales, in the final years of traditional steelmaking. Through raw, poetic storytelling and evocatively shot on 16mm film it weaves together the voices of generations to celebrate a way of life on the brink of vanishing.

item.title: The AI Doc: Or How I Became an Apocaloptimist (Netflix)
item.description: Directed by Daniel Roher. A father-to-be tries to figure out what is happening with all this AI insanity, and explores the most powerful technology humanity has ever created... and what's at stake if we get it wrong.

item.title: James McNeill Whistler
item.description: Directed by David Bickerstaff. Tate Britain is now holding the first major retrospective of Whistler in three decades. This blockbuster exhibition promises to reawaken the world to just how important Whistler is to art history, uniting world-famous masterpieces with rarely seen works. Exhibition on Screen will bring these stunning works and the incredible story behind them to cinemas around the world while the exhibition is still running, bringing this truly global artist to a global audience. This will be an unmissable chance to get to know this visually spectacular artist and the influence he has had on those who followed.

item.title: Liberté, la statue qui voulait changer le monde (ARTE)
item.description: Directed by Julien Johan.

item.title: Everything Happens All the Time
item.description: Directed by Simon King. Through twenty-seven interviews, street footage, and photographs, this film explores the relationship between street photographers, their practice, and one another in the community that has formed around the genre in London.

item.title: You Had to Be There: How the Toronto Godspell Ignited the Comedy Revolution... (Greenwich Entertainment)
item.description: Directed by Nick Davis. Martin Short, Eugene Levy, Gilda Radner, Victor Garber, Paul Shaffer, and other entertainment icons got their start in a 1972 Toronto production of the musical Godspell. Featuring interviews with the surviving cast members, Lin-Manuel Miranda, Mike Myers, and more, the film recounts a pivotal moment in comedy history, in hilarious, moving, and inspiring detail. Executive produced by Judd Apatow.

item.title: Pulp: What Do You Do for an Encore? (MUBI)
item.description: Directed by Garth Jennings. A fusion of the brilliantly choreographed stage spectacle of Pulp’s biggest ever arena show — part of the global tour for More, the band’s first album in 24 years — with four decades of colorful, never-seen-before archival material.

item.title: George Clarke’s Amazing Spaces: First Homes
item.description: Britain is in the grip of a housing crisis, with many people unable to afford a traditional bricks-and-mortar home. George and his long-time collaborator Will Hardie meet the proactive and determined people finding creative ways to create a place they can call home. From buses and boats to former toilet blocks and tiny homes, the series follows couples and families transforming unexpected spaces into affordable homes of their own.

item.title: The Cycle of Love
item.description: Directed by Orlando von Einsiedel. Explores the romantic journey of PK Mahanandia, a Delhi street artist who trekked 6,000 miles by bicycle in 1977, venturing across continents to reunite with the woman he loved.

item.title: Dead Wife Cult
item.description: Directed by Josh Heaps. The life of cult icon Zoë Lund, through the eyes of her widower and an avid fan.

item.title: Schloss Schönbrunn - Hinter der Fassade der Macht (ARTE)
item.description: Directed by Klaus T. Steindl.

item.title: English Ultraviolence
item.description: Directed by Jake Hanrahan. Heavy Weekend 01: Underground “no rules” fight clubs are spreading fast across Europe, organised in secret and hidden from the authorities. No tickets, no spectators, no public locations. This isn’t bare-knuckle boxing. Eye-gouging, biting, stamping, head-butts and choking are all allowed. It’s not sport—it’s organised ultraviolence. Hanrahan attends one of the UK’s first no-rules fight clubs to find out why young men are risking it all on the concrete.

item.title: Yeah Yeah Yeahs: Hidden in Pieces
item.description: Directed by Barnaby Clay. Indie-rock group the Yeah Yeah Yeahs channel the spirit of David Lynch with this exquisitely ethereal, sublimely surreal record of a Los Angeles concert performance.

item.title: Siren: The Voices of Shelley Beattie (HBO Documentary Films)
item.description: Directed by Irene Taylor. Shelley Beattie, a Deaf woman and champion bodybuilder, found fame in the 1990s on the hit TV show American Gladiators, where she competed under the name "Siren" before her untimely death in 2008. While charismatic, gorgeous, and a fierce competitor, Beattie also battled personal demons, struggling with mental illness, addiction, and questions of her own identity. Framed by the insight of another Deaf woman in Hollywood who found herself in the spotlight at the same time, Academy Award-winning actress Marlee Matlin, the documentary unpacks the story of Shelley "Siren" Beattie and her complex legacy entwined with beauty, mental illness, and love.

item.title: Boundless: The Man Who Became Human
item.description: Directed by Caleb Applegate. Ben Greenfield taught millions how to master the body. This is the story of everything that mastery could not reach. What remains when a man can no longer outrun himself?

item.title: Boorman and the Devil
item.description: Directed by David Kittredge. Featuring commentary from surviving participants, as well as other filmmakers and critics, this documentary chronicles the career of director John Boorman and the tumultuous production of his film Exorcist II: The Heretic, exploring its critical and commercial failure, how it changed the industry, and the importance of risk-taking in art.

item.title: Out of Breath
item.description: Directed by George T. Nierenberg. OUT OF BREATH shines the spotlight on the human cost paid by people living with sleep apnea and their loved ones. Yet, for all the darkness they face there is also light at the end of the tunnel as their hope, courage, and perseverance brings them closer to the promise of successful treatment.

item.title: The Hammer (Submarine Entertainment)
item.description: Directed by Simon Wallon. Simon de Pury is a familiar face in the art world. The former chairman of Sotheby’s has a larger-than-life personality and is known as the «Mick Jagger of auctions.»

item.title: LINKIN PARK: UNSHATTER
item.description: Directed by Joe Hahn. After a seven-year hiatus following the devastating loss of their beloved bandmate Chester Bennington, LINKIN PARK'S remaining members struggled to find their way forward. Their shared history and enduring friendship, combined with the fresh perspective of two new band members Emily Armstrong and Colin Brittain spark a renewed creative energy that leads them on a transformative journey of artistic reinvention. Following the band from intimate 2022 studio sessions through their explosive FROM ZERO album release and concert in São Paulo, this documentary weaves together rare vault footage, electrifying performances from sold-out shows, and candid interviews with band members and fans—capturing the raw, honest story of what it means to start over.

item.title: The Fighting Dinosaurs
item.description: Directed by David James Armsby.

item.title: The Last First: Winter K2
item.description: Directed by Amir Bar-Lev. A historic race to become the first to summit K2 in winter unravels into tragedy, exposing how ambition, ego, and the pursuit of glory can be as dangerous as the mountain itself.

item.title: Knife: The Attempted Murder of Salman Rushdie
item.description: Directed by Alex Gibney. In 2022, Salman Rushdie was preparing to deliver a lecture on the United States as a safe haven for writers when a man rushed the stage and, in 27 seconds, stabbed him 15 times. Airlifted to hospital, Rushdie survived, barely, and his wife Rachel Eliza Griffiths began filming immediately, capturing an unfiltered view of his recovery, return to life and how he regained his spirit and hope for the future.

item.title: Secrets of the Southwest: Science Behind the Secrets
item.description: Meet the inspiring individuals and communities who work to protect our most beloved UK wildlife.

item.title: Try!
item.description: Directed by Oisín Mistéil. Four Irish Rugby teams who defy stereotypes tackle their way to the Mixed Ability Rugby World Cup, where full-contact sport meets joyful belonging.

item.title: Secrets of the Southwest
item.description: Discover the hidden stories Britain's southwest has to offer. From Foxes fighting on the streets of Bristol to Puffins looking for love on Skomer Island.

item.title: Travel Reminiscence
item.description: Directed by Barney Gibbons. At a London community centre, facilitators and volunteers run a travel-themed session for people living with dementia and their families, friends and carers. Together, the group embarks on a playful journey: discussing past trips, revisiting these through theatre, and writing postcards to loved ones.

item.title: The Dance of the Kokorrdit
item.description: Directed by Elio B Cunampio. A Wounaan teenager and a leader of their community venture into the Darién in search of a sacred bird. Along the way, they will face the dangers that threaten their territory and their culture.

item.title: Musk (HBO Documentary Films)
item.description: Directed by Alex Gibney. An incisive look behind the legend of Elon Musk, the world’s most heralded 'inventor-entrepreneur' who has enormous influence on the world in which we all live.

item.title: André Leon Talley — Style is Forever (Greenwich Entertainment)
item.description: Directed by Zach Stafford. André Leon Talley was a trailblazing fashion icon whose influence spanned nearly five decades. This documentary explores his legacy of inclusivity, elegance, and the fearless pursuit of authenticity. Interviews with Anna Wintour, Tom Ford and Diane von Furstenberg, among others, as well as never-before-seen footage, reveal Talley’s personal and professional challenges and remarkable triumphs.

item.title: Lesbian Lines
item.description: Directed by Cara Holmes. In a silenced Ireland, a community of lesbians builds an underground network of helplines - offering connection, survival, and defiance through the simple act of answering the phone.

item.title: Everest: The Other Side (National Geographic Documentary Films)
item.description: Directed by Jimmy Chin. An intimate portrait of two people bound by love, ambition, and the pursuit of the impossible. Elite ski mountaineers Jim Morrison and Hilaree Nelson fell deeply in love while reaching the pinnacle of their sport. Their drive sharpened into a shared dream: to climb and ski the direct North Face of Mount Everest - the most difficult and dangerous climb on the mountain and the most coveted ski line on Earth - something only a handful have ever achieved, and no one has successfully skied down.

item.title: Transformation
item.description: Directed by Ganna Tretiak. A feature-length documentary exploring the profound inner metamorphosis of Ukrainian civilians from the creative sector who chose to enlist as soldiers to defend their country. The film maps the deep psychological and lifestyle shifts experienced by musicians, artists, and filmmakers as they stepped away from civilian art to enter the realities of war.

item.title: Carl Sagan: We Are Made of Star Stuff (National Geographic Documentary Films)
item.description: Directed by Nanette Burstein. Serving as an intimate and cinematic portrait of Sagan, the Untitled Carl Sagan Documentary will explore his love story with partner Ann Druyan and with science. The film will include exclusive audio recordings, archival clips and animation, along with interviews with his family, friends and colleagues. With the full support of Sagan’s family and friends, the film will present a fascinating look into the life and career of one of the world’s most inspiring and revolutionizing scientists of our time.

item.title: Forza on the Run
item.description: Directed by Jake Hanrahan. Heavy Weekend 02: The French police have put the illegal drift racers of Paris on final notice, so they've took off on the run across the border into Belgium. Hanrahan rides along with the crew as they dodge police and takeover Brussels.

item.title: Back to the Beginning: Ozzy's Final Bow
item.description: Directed by Ben Wainwright-Pearce. A powerful return to roots, this concert captures Black Sabbath in peak form - reuniting to deliver classic hits with raw energy and legendary precision.

item.title: Don't Let The Bastards Grind You Down
item.description: Directed by Christoph Farwig. "Don't Let The Bastards Grind You Down" is a documentary film about British social policy. The focus is on the political struggle against neoliberal austerity policies, which have their origins in the hated Thatcher government. The film features the former socialist MP Dave Nellist, who is now the national chair of the Trade Unionist & Socialist Coalition and Hannah Sell, the general secretary of the Socialist Party. The film features a local election campaign in the miners' town of Nuneaton, students campaigning against an increase in tuition fees and refuse workers from Birmingham striking against massive cuts to their wages.

item.title: Finding Faith
item.description: Directed by Mary McCartney. A short film contextualising the cultural significance of George Michael's Faith Tour via unheard interview voice-over, unseen images by Herb Ritts, and behind-the-scenes footage of the Faith music video.

item.title: George Michael: The Faith Tour
item.description: Directed by Andy Morahan. A stunning delve into George Michael's 1988 Faith Tour, as shot live at the famous Palais Omnisports de Paris-Bercy. This exclusive footage, assembled from a 14-camera shoot captured on 35mm over two nights (30–31 May 1988), features the 24-year-old pop star at the height of his powers.

item.title: Making Marie Antoinette
item.description: Directed by Eleanor Coppola. Eleanor Coppola's behind-the-scenes documentation of her daughter Sofia Coppola directing the 2006 film Marie Antoinette, capturing the craftsmanship and challenges of being a young female director.

item.title: Whiddy (ARTE)
item.description: Directed by Adrian McCarthy. A small rural community in Ireland welcomes in a major, global oil company with open arms but just 10 years and numerous oil spills later, that dream turns into an unimaginable nightmare. 50 lives lost in a tragedy that silenced and divided the community and still haunts it to this day.

item.title: 1 in 2
item.description: Directed by David Wilkinson. Nearly one in two of us will be diagnosed with cancer at some point in our lives. David Nicholas Wilkinson is one of them, twice over. In 2020, a colonoscopy found his bowel to be extremely healthy for a man his age. In 2023, a FIT test came back clear and, like almost everyone who takes one, he assumed that meant the all-clear. In 2024, a second colonoscopy found bowel cancer. Stage 4. He was told his tumour was 5-6 years old. What went wrong? A FIT test looks for blood. Wilkinson’s tumour never bled. Nor do a great many others. 1 IN 2 follows Wilkinson through his own treatment, where he discovers a steep rise in bowel cancer among people far too young to be screened for it, and far too young, it seems, to be believed. Among those who tell him their stories is a bowel surgeon whose own symptoms were dismissed by her oncologist colleagues and in part by herself because she was only 44.

item.title: The Neighbourhood is Changing
item.description: Documentary on the making and legacy of Mulberry Street featuring new interviews with cast and crew

item.title: American Doctor
item.description: Directed by Poh Si Teng. When three heroic American doctors — Palestinian, Jewish, and Zoroastrian — enter Gaza to save lives in the middle of a genocide, they find themselves caught between medicine and politics, risking everything to expose the truth.

item.title: Phantom 814
item.description: Directed by Jake Hanrahan. Heavy Weekend 03: Unique access to the most mysterious organisation in France. Jake Hanrahan travels with the bizarre syndicate known as "814SSR". They shoot guns, host fight clubs, and make money in the underground. Yet still, they insist they're not a gang and are simply doing hardcore trolling. The truth? Decide for yourself...
